scenes.headline: SparkSession
scenes.subtitle: The single entry point to all Spark functionality.
scenes.narration: The SparkSession is the unified entry point you use to access every feature of Spark in modern PySpark.

scenes.headline: Why it matters
items: One object for DataFrames, SQL, and configuration
Replaces the older tangle of separate contexts
Created once and reused across your whole application
getOrCreate returns the existing session if one exists
scenes.narration: The SparkSession gives you one object for DataFrames, SQL, and configuration. It replaces the older tangle of separate contexts, is created once and reused throughout your application, and getOrCreate safely returns an existing session.

scenes.headline: Building a session
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = (SparkSession.builder
    .appName("SalesETL")
    .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
    .getOrCreate())

df = spark.read.csv("/data/sales.csv", header=True)
scenes.narration: We use the builder to name the app and set a configuration, then call getOrCreate to obtain the session. From that session we immediately read a CSV into a DataFrame, showing how the session is the gateway to everything.

scenes.headline: Session as gateway
scenes.narration: From the single SparkSession you can read data, run SQL queries, and manage configuration — it is the gateway to the entire API.

scenes.text: Create one SparkSession per application and pass it everywhere you need Spark.
scenes.narration: As a rule, create one SparkSession per application and reuse it everywhere rather than building new ones.
